questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they cannot turn right. It is a regulation sign that drivers must obey.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a center lane for left turns only. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and makes you slower to react. It also impairs your judgment, which are both dangerous when driving.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, near railroad crossings, or on bridges. Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights. Do not pass in any no passing zone.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror as you slow down. Move to the left lane before the intersection. Make sure your path is clear of traffic and pedestrians before turning.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. This includes changing lanes, leaving a parking space, entering traffic from a parking area or alley, and passing other vehicles.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle signal. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to create a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down and make room for the emergency vehicle. Stop and let it pass. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge into traffic?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. Check your mirrors and blind spots to find a safe gap. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing warning sign alerts you that a train may be coming. Obey all railroad signs and never go around lowered barriers.

questions.question: You must stop for a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if the pedestrian is on your side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian is in a clearly marked crosswalk.
If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
Only if a "Walk" signal for pedestrians is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians crossing at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Let them cross safely before you drive.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal a lane change.
Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To change lanes safely, signal first, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out as you are driving, you should:

options.text: Brake hard immediately.
Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal slowly. Once you have control, brake gently and pull to a safe spot.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A deaf person.
A person involved with a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind. You must always yield to blind pedestrians.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.
Require less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and heavier, so they need more distance to stop than smaller cars.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to get a ride from someone who has not been drinking. Coffee and showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. The body needs about an hour to process one drink.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: To avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Never pass them.
Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
Flash your lights at them.
Sound your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on their sides and behind them. Do not drive next to them or too close behind them.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the light like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the light like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop, just like a stop sign. It warns of a dangerous intersection.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Stop and back up.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours is like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: When a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance cards.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A serious traffic safety problem.
questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious traffic safety problem. Safe driving is impossible when you drink alcohol or take drugs. Driving under the influence endangers you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit. When conditions are poor, slow down.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: The DMV's Driver Improvement Program promotes safety by:

options.text: Suspending licenses for 30 days for drivers 18 or older with four traffic convictions in 24 months.
Suspending licenses for six months for drivers under 18 with three traffic convictions.
Restricting licenses for 90 days for drivers under 18 with two traffic convictions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers with multiple traffic convictions or accidents may face penalties. Drivers 18 and older get a 30-day suspension for four convictions in 24 months. Drivers under 18 get a 90-day restriction for two convictions or a six-month suspension for three convictions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road is one-way and you cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to signal that you are turning.

options.text: Your horn.
Your headlights.
Hand signals.
Your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show other drivers that you are turning.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.
